# What is the configuration issue and calling method that the original thread confirmed when the Pinocchio single pendulum ABA goes from expected -4.905 to -7.7?

> **Current answer:** Maintainer pointed out that the original code forgot to normalize the configuration. The model uses continuous joints, parameterized as [cos(theta), sin(theta)], so normalization should be applied before ABA, and the returned value must be re-assigned to q. The thread did not provide the corrected acceleration output or revert to a full walking model retest, so this can only be considered as a confirmed input correction, and not as a resolution to the complete swing leg issue.

## Key terms

- Continuous joint (连续关节)
- Configuration manifold (配置流形)
- Configuration normalization (构型归一化)
- Joint acceleration (关节加速度)
- Articulated-Body Algorithm, ABA (关节空间前向动力学算法)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why should we check continuous-joint configuration normalization when the ABA gives an acceleration larger than the analytical expectation?
- Single pendulum length 2, mass 1, moment of inertia 1, gravity 9.81, center of mass to pivot distance 1; at pi/2 zero velocity initialization, original author expected -4.905, but ABA gave -7.7.
- In a larger walking model, the original author first observed swing-leg joint accelerations that were too large and inconsistent with other solvers.

## Environment

- pinocchio3-preview, Python, attachment single_pendulum.urdf; original post did not provide OS, specific commit, or build options.

## Priority diagnostics

- Check URDF joint type and model.nq/model.nv; continuous joints cannot be filled with a single scalar angle directly.
- Normalize q before calling ABA/constraintDynamics, and retain the returned value.

## Possible causes

- Maintainer pointed out that the original q was not normalized; the continuous joint uses [cos(theta), sin(theta)] parameterization.

## Attempts

- Original author simplified from walking constraintDynamics to a single pendulum ABA and provided Python code and URDF.
- Maintainer provided a complete script snippet with q = pin.normalize(model, q).

## Effective fixes

- Use q = pin.normalize(model, q) to receive the normalized value, then call pin.aba; do not only call normalize and discard the return value.

## Result

- Maintainer identified the issue as unnormalized configuration, explained that continuous joints are parameterized as [cos(theta), sin(theta)], and the original author did not publish the corrected values.

## Limitations

- The thread did not provide the original author's normalized -4.905 reference, nor revert to a full walking/constraintDynamics model retest, so the complete swing leg issue still needs to be verified separately.
- This card cannot attribute all large accelerations to configuration normalization; inertial, units, external forces, and constraints also need independent verification.
- The attached code/URDF was not re-run in the current environment.

## Safety notes

- Before real-time WBC, check if the configuration manifold is valid and has finite values; large accelerations should not be directly converted to torque.
